state.never-started: svrngs is installed but hasn't run here yet
help.stopped: Your people can't reach what you lend until it runs again.
help.never-started: Run svrngs once in a terminal to join or start a group.
help.not-installed: svrngs isn't on this computer yet.
here.title: On this computer
here.none: Nothing else is running here to lend. Start your app, then open this again.
lend.question: Lend %1 to %2?
lend.meaning: Everyone in %1 can open it as themselves, while this computer is on. You can stop any time.
lend.name: Name
lend.through: %1 only passes this port on, from a container or another program.
lend.known: Say its own name in one word. svrngs knows these: %1.
models.title: Models your people lend
models.none: Nobody in your groups lends a model yet.
models.quiet: None of your people's lends answered as a model just now. Their computer may be off.
models.copied: Copied %1, its OpenAI-compatible address. Play is on for it: an app on this computer can use it with no key, and if the app asks for one, type any text. Press Stop to turn Play off.
play.question: Turn on Play for %1?
play.meaning: Play lets any program of yours on this computer use %1 from %2 as you, with no key, and whatever %2 lends as %1 later too, until you press Stop here or on your home page. It gives no say in your groups, and lets no other account on this computer in.
play.apart: Play is on: any program of yours on this computer can use what %2 lends as %1, until you press Stop.
play.onPort: Play is on, at a port: any program on this computer can use it, another account's too, until you press Stop.
play.nobody: someone none of your groups names now
models.playing: Play is on: any program of yours here can use it
models.unplayed: Stopped: Play is off for it.
groups.title: Your groups
here.notRunning: Not running now: start it, and your people can open it
here.unlisted: Not shared: svrngs can't read this lend. Stop it, then lend it again.
here.heldAnother: Closed: what answers on its port isn't what you chose to share
here.heldUnjudged: Closed: svrngs can't tell what is answering on its port
here.heldUnapproved: Closed until you choose what it shares
here.heldUnknown: Closed by svrngs. Its home page says why
here.approveWhy: svrngs now keeps each share to the program you approve.
here.nowNothing: Its program isn't running. Start it, then keep sharing it here.
here.nowOther: What answers on its port now can't be shared from here.
here.nowAccount: Now answering: %1. Only your own programs can be shared from here: stop that one and start yours, or press Stop and lend yours again.
here.nowUnread: svrngs couldn't read what answers on its port. Open this panel again to look again.
keep.question: Keep sharing %1 with %2?
keep.meaning: Now answering: %1. Everyone in %2 can open it as themselves, while this computer is on.
keep.changed: What answers on %1's port changed after you pressed Keep sharing it, so nothing was approved. Press Keep sharing it again to see what answers now.
invite.question: Anyone with a new link can join %1 for a day, while this computer is on. It stops the last link you made here letting new people in; links others made still work, and everyone already in stays.
find.placeholder: Type to find an app, a model or a person
find.none: Nothing in your groups is called “%1”
groups.shared: Each opens as you, %1, on the computer that lends it, while it's on.
get.meaning: This downloads svrngs and its installer from svrngs's latest release, checks both against the svrngs release key, and installs svrngs for you alone, with no password. It puts svrngs in ~/.local/bin, runs it as your user service whenever you log in, adds it to your applications menu, and adds ~/.local/bin to your shell's startup file if your terminal doesn't look there yet. Then your browser opens your home page, where you can start a group or join one.
get.over: It replaces the older svrngs here, and keeps your groups and what you lend.
get.link: Invite link, if a friend sent you one
get.name: Your name there
get.joins: With this link, svrngs joins that group right away, as %1, before your home page opens. Everyone in the group sees that name.
